planting.note: Set out container-grown plants after the last frost once soil has warmed, since root disturbance and cold, wet soil are both poorly tolerated.

directions: Plant in full sun in lean, acidic, extremely well-drained sandy or gravelly soil, and avoid phosphorus-rich fertilizers as with all Proteaceae. Mimetes cucullatus, known as the Cape pagoda, is a distinctive Western Cape fynbos shrub whose small, inconspicuous flowers are tucked within tiers of leafy, hood-shaped bracts that flush brilliant red to orange through the winter and spring flowering season, giving the plant its tiered, pagoda-like look rather than relying on showy blooms themselves. It is slow to reach flowering size and, like many fynbos Proteaceae, is adapted to a fire-prone landscape where mature plants are often killed by fire and the population regenerates afterward from a long-lived soil seed bank. Grow it in a Mediterranean-climate garden with dry summers and winter rainfall, siting it where winter cold stays mild since it has only moderate frost tolerance.
